source.title: Belfast News-Letter, 5 July 1930, p. 5 ("Antrim County Council: meeting of the Proposal Committee"); Belfast News-Letter, 8 May 1930, p. 7 ("Local elections in Ulster: no contests for seats on Antrim County Council; list of nominations"); Northern Whig, 5 May 1927, p. 8 ("Antrim County Council: nominations for the triennial elections; four contests likely")
source.publisher: Belfast News-Letter (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: returned unopposed: no nomination was received for the division and the retiring member continued (Belfast News-Letter, 8 May 1930, p. 7); named as a sitting member of the new council early in the term (Belfast News-Letter, 5 July 1930, p. 5: 'on the motion of Mr. John Kinnear, seconded by Mr. William Shaw, Mr. John P. M'Cann was re-elected vice-chairman' of the committee)

note: Triennial election of Antrim County Council on the 23 county electoral divisions; nominations received by Andrew (Alexander) Millar, secretary, at the County Courthouse, Belfast, on 7 May 1930, and there were no contests in any division (Belfast News-Letter, 8 May 1930). No poll was therefore held: the statutory election day was Thursday 5 June 1930, the day fixed for the local elections that year (Belfast municipal polling '5th June', Belfast News-Letter, 7 May 1930, p. 9; guardians election 'Thursday, 5th June', Irish News, 30 April 1930, p. 6). The queue's provisional 29 May is not supported by any source seen. The News-Letter prints no party labels and no sitting-member asterisks, so neither is given. Added from reports of the new council's meetings early in the term, each division inferred from the previous return: Dunminning, Kirkinriola and Glenarm. division inferred from the 2 June 1927 return (John Kinnear; Northern Whig, 5 May 1927, p. 8); the Belfast News-Letter, 5 July 1930, p. 5 names the member as sitting for the new council (quarterly meeting of the Proposal Committee of Antrim County Council, Ballymena Courthouse, Friday 4 July 1930). Deemed re-elected (no nomination).
